final_rationale: The verdict does not change because the Actor supplied no new admissible evidence and mainly reframed the same record more narrowly. That reframing is partly persuasive in one respect: it correctly limits the claim to a disclosure-based certification theory and concedes that clean certification is unsupported. But the governing policy requires more than a narrow theory. It requires evidence that the current release documentation already reflects current evaluation results and that the material segment weakness is disclosed or covered by approved mitigation. On the present record, those predicates are still unproven. This is why the case does not rise to compliant_with_caveats: a caveat can narrow an otherwise supportable certification, but here the caveat itself depends on missing documentary proof. The packet therefore remains suspicious rather than compliant, because the claimed certification posture is still conditional on evidence not actually in the record.
remaining_concerns: No new admissible evidence was provided that the current release documentation actually reflects the latest evaluation results.
No admissible current model-card or release-record excerpt shows the required disclosure of the clinical coding assistant weakness.
There is still no approved mitigation or reviewed risk acceptance in evidence for the material segment weakness.
The actor's narrowed position remains conditional on documentation that is not in the record; that is an unresolved compliance predicate, not merely a caveat.
Prior approval and informal monitoring remain contextual only and cannot close the evidentiary gap for current-release certification.
